ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a black film capacitor, with “CL21” and “250V105J” clearly marked on the casing. Reasoning: The question asks for the nominal capacitance of the capacitor, not the rated voltage or tolerance. In the marking, “250V” indicates the rated voltage, and “J” usually indicates the tolerance code; the three-digit code “105” is used to indicate the capacitance. According to the capacitance code rule, “105” means the first two digits are 10, and the third digit 5 means multiplied by 10^5, with the unit pF, so the capacitance is 10 × 10^5 pF = 1,000,000 pF. Since 1,000,000 pF = 1 μF, the nominal capacitance of this capacitor is 1 μF.
